rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html Proposition 4.3 and its proof (lines 269-277): c = sqrt(pi/2)/e = 0.46107; z* with p = 1/e; u(z) = -ln p - c(z + 1/z) >= 0 for 0 < p <= 1/e

Mills-ratio bounds (Lemma 2.2): x phi(x)/(1 + x^2) <= Q(x) <= phi(x)/x give phi(z) <= Q(z)(z + 1/z) and phi(z)/Q(z) >= z, so e^(-z^2/2) = sqrt(2 pi) phi(z) <= sqrt(pi/2) p (z + 1/z) and it suffices that u(z) = -ln p - c(z + 1/z) >= 0 (page's steps; -ln p = -ln 2 - ln Q, Q' = -phi, so u' = phi/Q - c(1 - 1/z^2)). u' >= z - c(1 - 1/z^2) > 0 for all z > 0 (for z < 1 the right side is negative; for z >= 1 it is below c < 1 <= z), so u is increasing. At p = 1/e, z* = 0.9004526 and u(z*) = 1 - c(z* + 1/z*) = 0.0727888 > 0 (scipy). The page's displayed arithmetic 1 - 0.46107 x 2.01101 = 0.0728 (exact 0.072789 -> 0.0728). For 0 < p <= 1/e, z >= z* so u(z) >= u(z*) > 0. rows.evidence: unchanged since 5a184d0 (git diff checked); round-27 evidence: Re-derived. Boole: 1 - H(z_B) <= sum_k P(|Z_k| > z_B) = K x 2(1 - Phi(z_B)) = K x alpha/K = alpha, so H(z_B) >= 1 - alpha and h <= z_B. The replacement sentence 'Apart from a small gain that exists even under independence, the gain comes from dependence' is now true and agrees with the Remark's next sentence and with Lab 4's interpretation: by quadrature over the common factor, the limiting sup-t value for equicorrelated normals is 3.0160 at rho = 0, 2.9805 at 0.3 and 2.4794 at 0.9, never above the independence value (Sidak's inequality for Gaussian vectors), so everything beyond the 0.007 gain at rho = 0 is due to dependence. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html lines 596-598 (equicorrelated normals are MTP2 for 0 <= rho < 1; one-sided p-values; the Simes step at line 598), Lab 5 hypothesis (line 638)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 5a184d0 (git diff checked); round-27 evidence: Re-derived at d10fb51. (a) Sigma = (1-rho) I + rho 11' with Sherman-Morrison: Sigma^{-1} = (1/(1-rho)) [I - rho 11'/(1-rho+m0 rho)], so the off-diagonal entries of Q are -rho/((1-rho)(1-rho+m0 rho)) <= 0 for 0 <= rho < 1. (b) For a normal density with precision Q, log f(z) = const - (1/2) z'Qz; with u = x v y and v = x ^ y, u_i^2 + v_i^2 = x_i^2 + y_i^2, so the diagonal terms cancel and log f(u) + log f(v) - log f(x) - log f(y) = (1/2) sum_{i != j} Q_ij (x_i x_j + y_i y_j - u_i u_j - v_i v_j). The bracket is 0 when (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) >= 0 and equals (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) <= 0 otherwise (checked in the four sign cases), so each term Q_ij times the bracket is >= 0 and f(u) f(v) >= f(x) f(y). Numerical spot check (num/simes_mtp2_check.out): 200,000 random pairs for each of (m, rho) = (3, 0.2), (5, 0.7), (10, 0.95), (20, 0): min(lhs - rhs) = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, -1.4e-14 (rounding), violations 0. (c) One-sided p-values are decreasing in z coordinatewise, which swaps join and meet, and the Jacobian is a product of one-coordinate factors that cancels because {u_i, v_i} = {x_i, y_i}: the true-null p-values are MTP2 as the page says. PASS.

rows.evidence: unchanged since 5a184d0 (git diff checked); round-27 evidence: Re-derived after the notation change. Dividing every constant of (3) by c = c(floor(gamma m) + 1) is (3) at alpha' = alpha/c (linear in alpha). Theorem 7.5 at level alpha' gives P(FDP > gamma) <= P(U_{l<=M} {q_(l) <= l alpha'/m0}). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Proposition 7.8 and proof (lines 600-607)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 5a184d0 (git diff checked); round-27 evidence: Re-derived after the rename A -> D. If the original procedure makes no false rejection, the augmented procedure rejects R = R0 + D' with D' = min(D, m - R0) <= D, at most D' of them false; R = 0 gives FDP = 0; otherwise FDP <= D'/(R0 + D') <= D/(R0 + D) because x -> x/(R0 + x) is increasing; and D <= gamma R0/(1 - gamma) iff D (1 - gamma) <= gamma R0 iff D <= gamma (R0 + D), so FDP <= gamma. Hence {FDP > gamma} needs a false rejection by the original procedure: probability <= alpha. Correct, and the letters D, D' no longer clash with the active set A.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html line 598 (new T span: 'In this design the Simes inequality also follows from Lesson 3 alone'); Lesson 3 Definition 5.1, Theorem 5.2, Proposition 5.3 (course/modules/S/S7/L03.html lines 262-282); Theorem 7.5 (L05.html lines 559-571)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 5a184d0 (git diff checked); round-27 evidence: Derivation, written out and checked: (1) Lab 5's true-null statistics are z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j with mu_j = 0 (the lab code: z = sqrt(rho) w + sqrt(1-rho) e + mu), p_j = 1 - Phi(z_j), rho in [0,1): this is Proposition 5.3's model restricted to the nulls, so the true-null p-values are PRDS on every subset (Definition 5.1). (2) Theorem 5.2's hypotheses hold for the family of the m0 true-null p-values (the family is all true nulls, so PRDS on the true nulls is PRDS on the family; each p_j is super-uniform because z_j ~ N(0,1) gives p_j ~ U(0,1); P(p_j <= u) = u > 0 for u > 0). Its bound FDR <= m0' q / m' with m' = m0' = m0 gives FDR <= q = alpha for BH at level alpha on the family. (3) When every hypothesis in the family is true, V = R, so FDR = E[1{R >= 1}] = P(R >= 1). (4) BH at level alpha on m0 p-values (step-up) rejects at least one hypothesis iff q_(l) <= l alpha/m0 for some l <= m0. Hence P(union_{l<=m0} {q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}) <= alpha: the Simes inequality for the true-null p-values. (5) Theorem 7.5 (containment {FDP > gamma} subset of union_{l<=M}{q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}, M <= m0, for the step-down with constants (3)) gives P(FDP > gamma) <= alpha for every rho in [0,1). Numerical check (num/simes_mtp2_check.py, seeded; output num/simes_mtp2_check.out): union frequency for m0 = 20, 100, 450 and rho = 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95 is between 0.0163 and 0.0508 (the largest, 0.0508 +- 0.0011 at m0 = 450, rho = 0, is the independent case where the Simes bound is exact at alpha; the difference from 0.05 is 0.7 se); BH any-rejection and the Simes union agree on the same draws (0.036 and 0.036, rho 0.5, m0 30). The paragraph's sentences are correct as written. Grade T: proved on the page from Lesson 3's proved results. The span carries no data-cite, as for the other proofs on the page (rows L05-math-thm31, L05-grade-remark65). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html line 330 ('Exchangeability is assumed, not justified. Bonferroni, Holm and BHY treat every hypothesis alike.') and the Section 6 normal-approximation paragraph
rows.evidence: unchanged since 5a184d0 (git diff checked); round-27 evidence: Classified at 3203b7e as definitional. 'Bonferroni, Holm and BHY treat every hypothesis alike' follows from Definition 2.1 and the step-down and step-up rules (the procedures use the p-values only through their ranks and the values of the statistics; the threshold of Bonferroni is the same at every step). 'Neither holds exactly for small samples, fat tails or serially correlated predictor returns' is a statement about the asymptotic normal approximation (Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.3 are asymptotic in the normal approximation; the MBF formula assumes the normal test statistic). Neither is an empirical or literature claim, so neither needs a span under the page's convention, and neither carries a number. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html Theorem 4.2 (lines 256-260, proof at 262-266) and the Problem P-solution at line ~405 (the same bound at π0 = 0.99)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 5a184d0 (git diff checked); round-27 evidence: Re-derived at bda7c27. Assumptions: Z ~ N(θ,1), H0: θ = 0, prior π_A on θ under the alternative (Definition 4.1). Step 1: φ(z−θ) ≤ φ(0) for every θ, so ∫φ(z−θ)π_A(dθ) ≤ φ(0) and B(π_A) = φ(z)/∫φ(z−θ)π_A(dθ) ≥ φ(z)/φ(0) = e^(−z²/2); the point mass at θ = z attains it. Step 2: posterior odds of H0 = PO·B(π_A) ≥ PO·e^(−z²/2); x ↦ x/(1+x) is increasing, so (4) holds. Numerical check (c096_check_r22.out): at z = 3, π0 = 0.99: PO = 99, x = PO·MBF = 1.099790657286, x/(1+x) = 0.523762049074; the threshold PO* = e^4.5 = 90.0171313005 gives π0* = 0.9890130574. Alternative priors (part B): B(π_A) ≥ MBF = 0.011108996538 for all 11 structured priors and all 2000 random discrete priors; the point mass gives B − MBF = 0 to floating point. Scope note checked: Definition 4.1 takes π_A as any prior on θ under the alternative and does not exclude θ = 0; on that reading the point mass δ_z attains the bound for every z, including z = 0 (B = 1 = e^0). If the alternative were meant to exclude θ = 0, attainment would hold for z ≠ 0 only, and the infimum would be approached, not attained, at z = 0; the Bayes figure at t = 0 shows the MBF as 1.00, which is the infimum on either reading. The proof's steps are complete and the assumptions are stated. PASS.
